investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-17T00:27–00:35Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are at capacity and preemption cannot free any slots. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~145–148 s), the agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produces an empty evidence object, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256–259). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two peer-pod-capable nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Supported by the identical scheduler message across all three sibling checks.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes are at capacity for any reason, scheduling always fails.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), reducing available capacity over time.
Lower confidence — a quota or limit object on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource at the namespace or node level that is set too low for concurrent eval probe traffic.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion Blocking All Remote Agent Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs could not complete, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod creation attempt times out (~145–147 s), which is the earliest failure boundary. This prevents the eval runner from ever reaching the state-polling phase, so all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) remain absent and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state is fully unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-17T00:27–00:35Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState — all four required evidence fields are missing, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across all eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two peer-pod-capable nodes are at capacity and preemption cannot free any slots. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~145–148 s), the agent never reaches a running/idle/ready state, and the eval runner produces an empty evidence object, violating the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256–259). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
